name: Palace
why: London skate label from 2009, the Tri-Ferg triangle on tees and tracksuits, dropped weekly; two US stores, New York and Los Angeles, founder-owned.
origin: Founded in 2009 in London, England by Lev Tanju (with Gareth Skewis, co-owner and CEO).

notes.tech: Thread proposed 2 (2026-10-11): Polartec 200 Series (3 styles); Pertex NetPlus recycled nylon (1 style); in the Winter 2026 range page but not in the store navigation: WINDSTOPPER by GORE-TEX LABS cargo parka, Pertex Quantum/Squared jackets — licensed (Polartec, Pertex, Gore); nothing owned; share of range 4 of 139 clothing styles (2.9%) carry a named licensed technical fabric. Seated as proposed, pending ruling.
notes.craft: Thread proposed 1 (2026-10-11): Palace names no factory, maker or mill and states no country of origin on any of 474 product pages; its Modern Slavery Statement says only that key factories it visited are in Vietnam, China, Hong Kong and Korea, and that it owns none. Fabric weights and gauges are stated, but no process. Borderline 2 if the statement's country list is counted as a made-in statement. Seated as proposed, pending ruling.

craft_evidence.owned: no: Modern Slavery Statement 2026 describes Tier 1 factories and suppliers it does not own; the group runs own fulfilment/warehousing (London, New Jersey) only
craft_evidence.makers: no: 0 of 474 PDPs (all clothing and footwear colourways) name a factory or maker
craft_evidence.mills: no: no mill named on any PDP; only licensed fabric brands (Polartec, Pertex) and YKK zippers
craft_evidence.madein: 0 of 474 PDPs state a country of manufacture; the Modern Slavery Statement names Vietnam, China, Hong Kong and Korea as where key factories were visited
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed: founded 2009 in London (Palace Skateboards Limited incorporated 15 Oct 2012, Companies House 08253929); no dated founding story on the store
craft_evidence.process: no: PDP technical bullets give fabric weights and gauges (10 oz canvas, 220gsm pique, 3-12 gauge knits), no making process
craft_evidence.reasoning: Palace names no factory, maker or mill and states no country of origin on any of 474 product pages; its Modern Slavery Statement says only that key factories it visited are in Vietnam, China, Hong Kong and Korea, and that it owns none. Fabric weights and gauges are stated, but no process. Borderline 2 if the statement's country list is counted as a made-in statement.

ownership.owner: GSLT Holdings Limited (Companies House 10560823, parent of the Palace Skateboards group), held by Levent James Tanju and Gareth Lloyd Skewis, each 25-50% (PSC register); GSLT holds 75%+ of Palace Skateboards Limited

opview: “I sit in front the TV with a takeaway and type on my iPhone absolute nonsense in bullet points and people find it funny” — Lev Tanju, founder, The Guardian, as quoted in Highsnobiety ("The Guardian Investigates How Palace Skateboards Blew Up", Brock Cardiner)
